docs.title: Corporate GHG Accounting under ISO 14064
docs.text: This site documents how [Organisation] prepares, controls, reports and assures its organisation-level greenhouse gas inventory.

docs.title: The process at a glance
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Set boundaries<br/>14064-1 cl. 5] --> B[Identify sources<br/>& assess significance]
    B --> C[Quantify<br/>14064-1 cl. 6]
    C --> D[Quality checks &<br/>uncertainty<br/>14064-1 cl. 8]
    D --> E[GHG report &<br/>GHG statement<br/>14064-1 cl. 9]
    E --> F[Verification<br/>14064-3]
    F -->|findings| C
    F --> G[Verification<br/>opinion]
    H[Targets &<br/>reduction plans] --> I[Validation<br/>14064-3]

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Read the principles and the ISO 14064 family overview.
  2. Agree the organisational boundary and reporting boundary.
  3. Follow the inventory management plan for the annual cycle.
  4. Prepare for verification.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Role Name Responsibility Inventory owner TBC Accountable for the GHG statement Inventory manager TBC Runs the annual cycle, maintains this repository Data owners TBC Supply and sign off activity data per source Internal reviewer TBC Independent check before verification Verification body TBC Accredited to ISO 14065

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Activity data A quantity of activity that causes emissions, such as kWh, litres or tonne-km. Base year The historical period chosen to compare emissions against over time. CO₂e Carbon dioxide equivalent. Converts each gas to the same unit using its GWP. Emission factor Converts activity data to emissions, such as kgCO₂e per kWh. GHG statement The organisation's factual, objective declaration that is the subject of verification or validation. GWP Global warming potential. Use 100-year values from one IPCC assessment report, and apply them consistently. Level of assurance How much confidence the verifier gives: reasonable (higher) or limited (lower). Materiality The size of an error or omission that could affect the decisions of intended users. Misstatement An error, omission or misreporting in the GHG statement. Organisational boundary Which facilities and entities are included, and how (control or equity share). Reporting boundary Which emission and removal sources are included. Significance Whether an indirect emission source is large or important enough to quantify. Verification Checking a statement about past events. Validation Checking the reasonableness of a statement about future events.

docs.title: The ISO 14064 family
docs.text: Standard Scope Used here for ISO 14064-1:2018 Quantifying and reporting GHG emissions and removals at organisation level The corporate inventory ISO 14064-2:2019 Quantifying GHG reductions from projects Out of scope, unless project-level credits are claimed ISO 14064-3:2019 Validation and verification of GHG statements Assurance of the inventory and of forward-looking claims ISO 14065:2020 Requirements for bodies that validate and verify Choosing an accredited verifier ISO 14066:2023 Competence of validation and verification teams Checking the verifier team ISO/TS 14064-4 Guidance on applying ISO 14064-1 Interpretation

docs.title: Verification vs validation
docs.text:
The two words are easy to confuse. In ISO 14064-3 the difference is about time:

Verification Validation Looks at Historical data and events Future-looking claims and assumptions Typical subject The annual GHG statement (e.g. "FY2025 emissions were 12,340 tCO₂e") A reduction target, transition plan or projected reductions Question asked Is the statement fairly stated and free of material misstatement? Are the assumptions, methods and limits reasonable and well supported? Covered in 05-verification 06-validation

docs.title: Relationship to the GHG Protocol
docs.text: ISO 14064-1 and the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard are compatible. ISO 14064-1:2018 groups emissions into six categories rather than three scopes. See the category-to-scope mapping.

docs.title: Accounting principles (ISO 14064-1, clause 4)
docs.text:
Every methodological decision in this repository should be traceable to one or more of these principles. Record the reasoning in the decision log.

Principle What it means in practice Relevance Choose sources, data and methods that suit the needs of the people who use the report. Completeness Include every relevant emission and removal. Justify every exclusion in writing. Consistency Use the same methods year on year so results can be compared. Document every change. Accuracy Reduce bias and uncertainty as far as is practical. Transparency Disclose enough information for a reader to make decisions with confidence.

docs.title: Verification and validation principles (ISO 14064-3, clause 4)
docs.text:
These apply to the verifier, but they shape what the organisation must provide.

Principle Implication for us Independence The internal reviewer must not have prepared the data they review. Ethical conduct — Fair presentation Report findings and limitations honestly. Due professional care — Professional judgement Expect the verifier to challenge estimates and assumptions. Evidence-based approach Every reported number must trace to evidence. See the evidence index.

docs.title: Selected base year
docs.text: Base year: TBC Reason for choice: TBC. Choose the earliest year with verifiable, complete data for all significant sources. Base-year inventory: inventory/<base-year>/, git tag <base-year>-verified

docs.title: Recalculation policy
docs.text:
Recalculate the base-year inventory (and every year since) when any of these changes the base-year total by more than the significance threshold of 5%, alone or added together:

Trigger Example Structural change Acquisition, divestment, merger, or moving activities in-house or outsourcing them Methodology change New calculation approach or improved emission factors Error discovery A significant error, or several errors that are significant together Boundary change New sources found to be significant

Do not recalculate for organic growth or decline, such as more production or more staff.

docs.title: Record of recalculations
docs.text: Date Trigger Impact on base year (tCO₂e, %) Approved by PR / tag

docs.title: Consolidation approach
docs.text:
Choose one approach and apply it to every entity:

Approach Rule Choose when Operational control 100% of emissions from operations we control operationally Most common. Aligns with where we can act. Financial control 100% of emissions from operations we control financially Aligns with financial reporting. Equity share Emissions in proportion to our ownership share Required by some joint-venture arrangements.

Selected approach: TBC Rationale: TBC (log it in the decision log)

docs.title: Entity and facility register
docs.text:
Maintain the register in inventory/<year>/boundary-register.csv (template: templates/boundary-register.csv). For each entity record:

  • legal name, country and ownership %
  • whether we hold operational and financial control
  • whether it is included, and the inclusion %
  • the reason for any exclusion

docs.title: Changes during the year
docs.text: Record acquisitions, disposals, mergers and outsourcing with their effective date. Check each against the base-year recalculation policy.

docs.title: Reporting boundary
docs.text:
ISO 14064-1:2018, clause 5.2

The reporting boundary sets out which emissions and removals are included. ISO 14064-1:2018 sorts them into six categories (see emission categories).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Direct emissions (Category 1). Quantify these in full. List every source: combustion, process, fugitive and land use.
  2. Indirect emissions from imported energy (Category 2). Quantify these in full.
  3. Other indirect emissions (Categories 3–6). Identify every source, then run the significance assessment. Quantify the significant ones.
  4. Exclusions. Record every source that is excluded, with the reason. This goes in the GHG report.

docs.title: Gases
docs.text: Include all seven Kyoto gases where relevant: CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, HFCs, PFCs, SF₆ and NF₃. Report each gas separately as well as in total CO₂e.

docs.title: Biogenic CO₂
docs.text: Report biogenic CO₂ emissions and removals separately from the category totals.

docs.title: Source register
docs.text: ID Category Source Gases Significant? Method Data owner C1-01 1 Natural gas boilers, Head office CO₂, CH₄, N₂O Yes (direct) Metered kWh × factor Facilities C1-02 1 Company vehicles CO₂, CH₄, N₂O Yes (direct) Fuel litres × factor Fleet C1-03 1 Refrigerant top-ups HFCs Yes (direct) Mass balance Facilities C2-01 2 Purchased electricity CO₂e Yes Metered kWh × factor (location & market) Facilities …

docs.title: Significance assessment for indirect emissions
docs.text:
ISO 14064-1:2018, clause 5.2.3

ISO 14064-1 asks the organisation to set its own pre-defined criteria for deciding which indirect emissions are significant. The criteria must be written down before the assessment and applied the same way every year.

docs.title: Criteria
docs.text:
Score each indirect source against each criterion. Any source that meets one or more criteria is significant and must be quantified.

# Criterion Threshold (set by us) 1 Magnitude. Estimated emissions are large compared with the total inventory. ≥ 1% of the estimated total 2 Level of influence. We can monitor and reduce the emissions. Yes / No 3 Risk or opportunity. The source creates climate-related financial, regulatory, supply-chain or reputational exposure. Yes / No 4 Sector guidance. Sector guidance treats the source as significant. Yes / No 5 Outsourcing. The activity used to be done in-house. Yes / No 6 Stakeholder interest. Intended users have said it matters. Yes / No

Use screening estimates (such as spend-based factors) for magnitude. Exclusions should add up to no more than 5% of estimated total emissions.

docs.title: Assessment record
docs.text:
Source ID Category Description Screening estimate (tCO₂e) Criteria met Significant? Justification C3-01 3 Business travel – air 1, 2 Yes C4-01 4 Purchased goods and services 1, 3 Yes C4-05 4 Waste — No Below threshold, low influence

Re-run the assessment every year, and whenever the business changes materially.

docs.title: Emission categories
docs.text:
ISO 14064-1:2018, clause 5.2.4

Cat. Name Typical sources 1 Direct GHG emissions and removals Stationary combustion (boilers, generators), mobile combustion (owned vehicles), process emissions, fugitive emissions (refrigerants), land use 2 Indirect emissions from imported energy Purchased electricity, heat, steam and cooling 3 Indirect emissions from transportation Upstream and downstream freight, employee commuting, business travel, client and visitor transport 4 Indirect emissions from products the organisation uses Purchased goods and services, capital goods, waste disposal, upstream energy (well-to-tank, T&D losses), leased assets 5 Indirect emissions linked to the use of the organisation's products Use of sold products, end-of-life of sold products, downstream leased assets, investments 6 Indirect emissions from other sources Anything not covered above

docs.title: Mapping to GHG Protocol scopes
docs.text:
ISO 14064-1 category GHG Protocol 1 Scope 1 2 Scope 2 3 Scope 3: categories 4, 6, 7, 9 4 Scope 3: categories 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 5 Scope 3: categories 10, 11, 12, 13, 15 6 Scope 3: anything else (for example, category 14 franchises, depending on context)

Some sources can sit in more than one place. Record the mapping used for each source in the source register, and keep it the same each year.

docs.title: Category 2: location-based and market-based
docs.text:
Report Category 2 both ways:

  • Location-based. Use the average grid factor for the country or region.
  • Market-based. Use supplier-specific factors, backed by contractual instruments such as REGOs or GOs, and residual-mix factors for everything else.

State which figure is used for the headline total and for targets.

docs.title: Emission factors
docs.text:
Keep every factor used in inventory/<year>/emission-factor-register.csv (template: templates/emission-factor-register.csv). Each factor needs:

  • a unique ID
  • its value, unit and the gases it covers
  • its source, publication year and table or row reference
  • its geography and period of validity
  • the GWP basis, if the factor is given in CO₂e

docs.title: Preferred sources
docs.text: Use Source UK fuels, electricity, travel, freight, waste UK Government GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting (DESNZ), for the reporting year Non-UK electricity (location-based) National inventory or IEA data Market-based electricity Supplier fuel-mix disclosure; residual-mix factors (such as AIB for Europe) Refrigerants GWPs from the selected IPCC assessment report Spend-based screening A recognised EEIO dataset (such as UK SIC-based, US EEIO or EXIOBASE). State the price year.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Use factors for the reporting year. If they are not yet published, use the latest available and disclose this.
  • Never change a factor in place. Add a new row and retire the old one, so that past calculations can be reproduced.

docs.title: General approach
docs.text:
For most sources:

Emissions (tCO₂e) = Activity data × Emission factor × GWP

Where the factor is already in CO₂e, no separate GWP step is needed.

docs.title: Hierarchy of methods
docs.text:
Use the most accurate method that is practical. Record the method used for each source in activity-data.csv (method_tier column).

Tier Method Example A Direct measurement Continuous emissions monitoring B Supplier-specific or primary activity data × specific factor Fuel invoices × fuel-specific factor; supplier-specific electricity factor C Primary activity data × published average factor kWh from meters × national grid factor D Estimated or modelled activity data × average factor Floor-area estimate of energy use E Spend-based (EEIO) £ spend × kgCO₂e/£

docs.title: Global warming potentials
docs.text: Selected GWP set: IPCC AR_ (100-year). Use one set throughout, and record it in the GHG report. If the set changes, recalculate the base year.

docs.title: Calculation rules
docs.text:
• Hold all calculations in version-controlled files. Never hard-code numbers in a report.
  • Use the same units throughout. Convert at the activity-data stage.
  • Every row of activity data must reference an evidence ID (see data quality).
  • Estimates and extrapolations, such as a missing month of meter data, must be flagged (is_estimate = TRUE) with the method described.

docs.title: Uncertainty assessment
docs.text:
ISO 14064-1:2018, clause 8.3

The organisation must assess the uncertainty of its GHG inventory, covering both activity data and emission factors.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
1. Give each source an uncertainty (±%) for its activity data and its emission factor. Base these on meter accuracy class, invoice versus estimate, or the uncertainty published with the factor.
  2. Combine the two for each source (error propagation, assuming they are independent): U_source = √(U_AD² + U_EF²)
  3. Combine across sources, weighted by emissions: U_total = √Σ(E_i × U_i)² / ΣE_i
  4. For large or skewed uncertainties, use Monte Carlo simulation instead.

docs.title: Qualitative rating
docs.text:
Where a number cannot be estimated, rate each source:

Rating Typical case Low (< ±5%) Billed, metered data with an official factor Medium (±5–20%) Partial estimates; average factors High (> ±20%) Spend-based; modelled or proxy data

docs.title: Use the results
docs.text: Focus improvement work on sources that are both large and highly uncertain. Record planned improvements in the inventory management plan.

docs.title: QA/QC checklist
docs.text:
Complete this for every reporting year, in inventory/<year>/qaqc-checklist.md.

  • Every entity in the boundary register has data, or a documented reason why not
  • Every significant source has activity data for all 12 months
  • Units are consistent; conversions have been checked
  • Emission factors match the register and are for the right year and geography
  • Estimates are flagged and their method is documented
  • Year-on-year change is over ±10% for a source → explained
  • Totals reconcile: source → category → inventory
  • Double counting checked (for example, fleet fuel cards against expense claims)
  • Category 2 reported location-based and market-based
  • Biogenic CO₂ reported separately
  • Sampled calculations recalculated by hand (at least 10%)
  • Internal reviewer sign-off recorded

docs.title: Evidence index
docs.text:
Every activity-data row must point to evidence (evidence_id). The index (inventory/<year>/evidence-index.csv) records:

  • evidence ID
  • description, such as "British Gas invoice Jan 2025, Site A"
  • where it is stored (path or link in the document store)
  • who provided it, and when

Verifiers sample from this index. A broken link is a finding.

docs.title: Methodology decision log
docs.text:
Record every judgement that affects the numbers. Verifiers will ask why.

ID Date Decision Options considered Rationale (principle) Impact (tCO₂e) Approved by D-001 Consolidation approach: operational control Operational / financial / equity Relevance: matches where we can act — D-002 GWP set: IPCC AR_ 100-yr AR5 / AR6 Consistency with factor dataset

docs.title: Annual cycle
docs.text: Month (FY end + n) Activity Owner Output −2 Review boundary, source register and significance assessment Inventory manager Updated registers −1 Brief data owners; issue data requests Inventory manager Data request log +1 Collect activity data and evidence Data owners activity-data.csv, evidence index +2 Calculate; QA/QC checks; uncertainty assessment Inventory manager Draft inventory +2 Internal review Internal reviewer Review record +3 Draft GHG report and GHG statement Inventory manager Draft report +3–4 Verification Verification body Findings, opinion +4 Fix findings; sign-off; publish Inventory owner Final report; git tag FYxxxx-verified

docs.title: Information management procedures (clause 8.1)
docs.text:
• Single source of truth. This repository holds methods, registers and calculations. Source evidence lives in the controlled document store at [location].
  • Change control. Every change is made by pull request and reviewed by someone other than the author.
  • Access. Write access is limited to the inventory team.
  • QA/QC checks before sign-off. See data quality.

docs.title: Document retention (clause 8.2)
docs.text: Keep the documents behind each verified inventory for at least 7 years, or longer if regulation or contracts require it.

docs.title: Improvement plan
docs.text: ID Source Issue Action Owner Target year Status IMP-01

docs.title: GHG report template
docs.text:
ISO 14064-1:2018, clause 9

Copy this outline for each year's report. Clause 9.3 of ISO 14064-1 lists the required and recommended content in full. Use it as the final checklist.

docs.title: 1. About the organisation
docs.text:
• Description of the reporting organisation
  • The person responsible for the report
  • The reporting period
  • Intended users and how the report will be published

docs.title: 2. Boundaries
docs.text:
• Organisational boundary and consolidation approach
  • Reporting boundary, with the criteria used to judge significant indirect emissions
  • Excluded sources, with reasons

docs.title: 3. Results
docs.text:
Category tCO₂e % of total 1. Direct 2. Imported energy (location-based) 2. Imported energy (market-based) 3. Transportation 4. Products used 5. Use of products 6. Other Total (state which Category 2 figure is used)
  • Results broken down by gas, and by facility or entity where relevant
  • Biogenic CO₂ emissions and removals, reported separately
  • GHG removals, if any

docs.title: 4. Methods
docs.text:
• Quantification methods, and changes since last year
  • Emission factors and GWPs used, with sources
  • Description of the uncertainty assessment, and its results

docs.title: 5. Base year and trends
docs.text:
• Base year and base-year emissions
  • Any recalculation, and the reason for it
  • Comparison over time

docs.title: 6. Reductions
docs.text:
• GHG reduction initiatives, and their effect, if quantified (clause 7)
  • Use of offsets or contractual instruments, disclosed separately

docs.title: 7. Assurance
docs.text:
• Whether the report was verified, by whom, and the level of assurance
  • A statement that the report was prepared in accordance with ISO 14064-1:2018

docs.title: GHG statement template
docs.text:
The GHG statement is what the verifier gives an opinion on. Keep it short and factual.

GHG statement of [Organisation] for the period [dd/mm/yyyy] to [dd/mm/yyyy]

[Organisation] has quantified its greenhouse gas emissions and removals in accordance with ISO 14064-1:2018 and the methods described in its GHG report dated [date].

tCO₂e Category 1: Direct emissions Category 2: Indirect emissions from imported energy (location-based) Category 2: Indirect emissions from imported energy (market-based) Categories 3–6: Other indirect emissions (significant sources) Total ([location / market]-based) Biogenic CO₂ (reported separately)

Organisational boundary: [operational control], covering [n] entities. Global warming potentials: IPCC AR[x], 100-year. Inventory version: git tag [FYxxxx-verified].

Signed: ____ Name / role: _ Date: _____

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Pre-engagement<br/>scope, criteria, assurance level,<br/>materiality, impartiality] --> B[Strategic analysis &<br/>risk assessment]
    B --> C[Evidence-gathering plan<br/>& sampling plan]
    C --> D[Verification activities<br/>site visits, document review,<br/>recalculation, interviews]
    D --> E[Findings raised]
    E --> F[Organisation corrects<br/>& responds]
    F --> G[Evaluation of the<br/>GHG statement]
    G --> H[Independent review]
    H --> I[Verification opinion<br/>& statement]

docs.title: What we agree with the verifier up front
docs.text:
Item Our position Subject GHG statement for FY____ covering Categories __ Criteria ISO 14064-1:2018 and this repository's documented methods Level of assurance Reasonable / Limited Materiality Quantitative threshold 5% of total (verifier's call, agreed in advance), plus qualitative factors Intended users Verification body accreditation ISO 14065 by [UKAS / other]

Reasonable or limited assurance?

  • Reasonable assurance needs more evidence. It is usually expected for Categories 1 and 2, and for regulatory or financing uses.
  • Limited assurance is common for Categories 3–6.

docs.title: What we provide
docs.text: Hand the verifier this checklist: the verification readiness checklist.

docs.title: Handling findings
docs.text:
• Log each finding as a GitHub issue using the Verification finding template, and in inventory/<year>/findings-log.csv.
  • Classify each one:
    • Non-conformity. The requirements are not met.
    • Misstatement. The numbers are wrong.
    • Observation. An improvement opportunity.
  • Fix each by PR, link the PR to the issue, and get the verifier to agree it is closed.
  • Uncorrected misstatements are added together and compared with the materiality threshold.

docs.title: Facts discovered after verification
docs.text: If an error is found after the opinion has been issued, tell the verifier. Then assess it against the base-year recalculation threshold.

docs.title: Verification readiness checklist
docs.text: Before the verifier arrives, confirm that each item exists and that its link works.

docs.title: Inventory design
docs.text:
• Organisational boundary and consolidation approach, with rationale
  • Boundary register: entities, ownership, control, inclusion
  • Source register for all six categories
  • Significance criteria and the assessment record
  • Base year, base-year inventory and recalculation policy

docs.title: Quantification
docs.text:
• Activity data for each source, every row linked to evidence
  • Emission-factor register with sources and versions
  • Calculation files that reproduce the reported totals exactly
  • Estimates flagged, with their methods
  • Uncertainty assessment

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Inventory management plan, with roles
  • Completed QA/QC checklist
  • Internal review record
  • Methodology decision log
  • Prior-year findings: every one closed or explained

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Draft GHG report (clause 9 content)
  • GHG statement signed by the responsible person
  • Git tag or commit hash of the version submitted for verification

docs.title: Logistics
docs.text:
• Data owners available for interviews
  • Site visit schedule agreed (where applicable)
  • Verifier has read-only access to the evidence store

docs.title: Validation of forward-looking claims
docs.text:
ISO 14064-3:2019

Validation assesses whether the assumptions, limits and methods behind a claim about the future are reasonable. For a corporate inventory, this typically applies to:

  • emission reduction targets (for example, "−42% Category 1 and 2 by 2030 compared with base year")
  • net-zero or transition plans
  • projected reductions from planned mitigation activities (ISO 14064-1, clause 7)

docs.title: What the validator assesses
docs.text: Area Questions Base-year link Is the target based on a verified base-year inventory? Boundary Does the target cover the same boundary as the inventory? Are exclusions disclosed? Assumptions Are the growth, grid-decarbonisation and technology assumptions reasonable and sourced? Methods Is the projection method appropriate and consistently applied? Ambition Is the target consistent with any framework claimed (such as SBTi criteria)? Monitoring Is there a plan to track progress and to verify it later?

docs.title: What we provide
docs.text:
• Target statement: scope, base year, target year, metric, absolute or intensity
  • Base-year inventory and its verification opinion
  • Projection model, with an assumptions register (value, source, sensitivity)
  • Planned mitigation actions, with estimated abatement
  • Monitoring and reporting plan

docs.title: Assumptions register
docs.text: ID Assumption Value Source Sensitivity (±tCO₂e) Owner A-01 Grid emission factor trajectory A-02 Business growth
